prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the continuous 3D geometry of the studio, showing a smooth brightness gradient along the white floor sheet extending from about 0.5 m below the camera wearer out to 2 m in front, flanked by a studio light stand and stepladder at 1.5–3 m on the right and a crouching photographer facing the wearer at 2.5–3 m on the front-left in front of a circular diffuser (3–3.5 m) and distant background people and furniture (4–5.5 m). Within arm's reach (0.2–0.5 m), the camera wearer's open notebook and right hand holding a pen appear as the brightest foreground surfaces at the bottom, alongside a seated person's legs and arms about 0.5 m to the bottom-left in frames 2 and 5. Across the five frames, as the camera wearer tilts their head downward and lifts the notebook to 0.2–0.3 m in frames 3–4 before lowering it to 0.4–0.5 m in frame 5, the bright foreground notebook plane expands to occlude the mid-ground floor and shifts the crouching photographer out of the top of the view. Compared to the RGB strip—where the uniform white floor backdrop and white notebook pages lack texture and blend together—the depth map clearly separates the tilted notebook plane from the underlying floor in frames 1, 2, and 5 and reveals the continuous ground slope. However, the depth map is unreliable on the brightly lit studio lamp on the far right (which saturates to pure white in frames 1, 2, and 5 as if at zero distance), merges the lifted notebook's upper edge into the white floor sheet in frames 3–4, and loses the thin tripod legs and distant background figures in the dark far field.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map outlines discrete regions across the studio layout, separating the foreground floor sheet and notebook from the crouching photographer facing the camera wearer at 2.5–3 m on the front-left, two distant standing people 4.5–5.5 m behind the photographer in frame 2, and studio equipment along the right side 1.5–3.5 m away. Within the camera wearer's arm's reach (0.2–0.5 m), it segments the wearer's right hand holding the pen at the bottom-right in frames 3–5 and left hand in frame 5, as well as the seated neighbor's legs and arm about 0.5 m to the bottom-left in frame 5. Across the sequence, as the camera tilts steeply downward and the raised notebook occludes the room in frames 3–4 before dropping back down in frame 5, the background masks exit the top of the frame while foreground person masks appear at the bottom, adding little beyond the RGB view except isolating the tiny, partially occluded standing figures at the top edge of frame 2. The map is highly unreliable in its semantic classifications and object boundaries: it merges the white notebook and floor backdrop into a single massive mask mislabeled as 'bed' in frame 2 and an unlabeled purple polygon in frames 3–4, misclassifies the crouching photographer as 'dog' and 'teddy bear' in frame 2, and labels the circular diffuser, studio light, and red stepladder as 'chair' (frames 1–2) or 'traffic light' and 'umbrella' (frame 5). It also completely misses the floor sheet and foreground notebook in frames 1 and 5, fails to detect the seated neighbor's limbs in frame 2, and omits the pen and thin tripod stands across all frames.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map isolates only the human keypoints of the crouching photographer located 2.5–3 m in front and slightly to the left of the camera wearer near the far edge of the white floor sheet. In frames 1 and 2, the compact yellow body skeleton shows the photographer squatting low to the floor with bent knees, elbows tucked in within arm's reach of their own upper body and camera, and head and shoulders angled directly toward the camera wearer. Across the five frames, as the camera wearer pitches their view downward toward the notebook, the photographer's skeleton shifts upward toward the top-left from frame 1 to frame 2, is clipped by the upper frame boundary to just a small cluster of foot keypoints at the top-left of frame 3, and disappears completely out of view in frames 4 and 5. Compared to the RGB strip, the skeleton overlay makes the photographer's folded limb geometry and forward-facing posture explicit despite dark clothing and occlusion of their face by the handheld camera. However, the map is unreliable everywhere else in the scene: it fails to detect any magenta hand skeletons—completely missing the camera wearer's own hands holding the notebook and pen at 0.2–0.5 m in frames 3–5—and misses both the seated person's legs and arms at 0.5 m on the bottom-left (frames 2 and 5) and the two standing people 4.5–5.5 m in the background (frames 1–2).
